calibration.reason: Clear labels and legibility support the task, but the familiar layout limits originality and misplaced focus after invalid input impairs recovery.

primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and show all three closures.
primary_action.observed: 6 m received visible focus; the list showed the path closing, ferry stopping and footbridge closing.

A-1440.edge_observation: ArrowRight wrapped to 2 m; the list contained only the riverside path closure.
A-1440.fact_check: The waterline aligns with the 6 m gauge mark and the three stated thresholds. Actual local closure thresholds are unsupported by a cited source.
A-1440.strength: The illustrated crossing and prominent controls connect the water level to the consequences.
A-1440.weakness: The large illustration extends below the desktop viewport, so its lower portion is cut off initially.
A-1440.repair: Reduce the desktop illustration height or adjust the layout so the full cross-section is visible alongside the result.

primary_action.expected: Wrap directly from 2 m to 6 m and show all three closures.
primary_action.observed: 6 m received visible focus and all three closures appeared. The complete list and illustration fit in the first 390 × 844 viewport.

A-390.edge_observation: ArrowRight wrapped back to 2 m; only the riverside path closure remained in the list.
A-390.fact_check: The waterline meets the 6 m mark, consistent with the selected level. Real-world thresholds are not independently substantiated.
A-390.strength: The controls and complete result are readable without scrolling.
A-390.weakness: The scaled-down gauge and crossing labels are quite small.
A-390.repair: Enlarge key gauge labels or simplify the illustration while retaining the complete result in view.

primary_action.input: Tab to the slider, then Tab through the three closure rows and Enter on the 6 m row
primary_action.expected: Set 6 m and show all three closures.
primary_action.observed: The value changed to 6 m; the path and footbridge were marked closed and the ferry stopped. The slider's arrow keys moved only 0.1 m per press.

B-1440.edge_observation: Shift+Tab twice and Enter on the 2 m row set 2 m. Only the path was marked closed; ferry and footbridge remained listed as level not reached.
B-1440.fact_check: The waterline aligns with the 6 m scale mark. Actual local thresholds are unsupported by a cited source.
B-1440.strength: The cross-section, scale and status rows form a clear, precise visual explanation.
B-1440.weakness: The rows look like status information, so their ability to set a level is not obvious; the slider's 0.1 m keyboard steps make a direct jump cumbersome.
B-1440.repair: Make the threshold shortcuts visibly actionable and provide an obvious keyboard shortcut or discrete level control.

primary_action.input: Tab four times, then Enter on the 6 m row
primary_action.expected: Set 6 m and show all three closures.
primary_action.observed: The level changed to 6 m and all three statuses were visible in the first 390 × 844 viewport.

B-390.edge_observation: Shift+Tab twice and Enter set 2 m. The path alone was marked closed; the ferry and footbridge rows remained visible as level not reached.
B-390.fact_check: The visible waterline reaches the 6 m scale mark, matching the text. Real-world closure thresholds are not independently substantiated.
B-390.strength: The entire cross-section, control and result fit within the first mobile viewport.
B-390.weakness: The result sits near the bottom of the viewport, and the threshold rows do not visibly announce that they are controls.
B-390.repair: Give threshold shortcuts a clear control affordance and add a little more vertical margin around the final row.

preference.reason: Both show consistent 6 m results and fit the complete mobile result in the tested viewport. A makes the discrete levels immediately apparent and reaches 6 m with one arrow key from its initial selection; B's threshold shortcuts are less discoverable and its slider advances in 0.1 m steps.

decision: The floodwall beats both paired controls but removes no limits from the score gate. Fix desktop framing and the phone label scale before evaluating the next iteration.
